text: Consistency check, flesh versus fur (Nick's tail question): the bare-body views now show the flesh under the fur, which is what the 3D blockout models and the rig moves. The cotton-ball tail is a short stub of flesh; its round shape comes from fur. The skull is smaller than the fluffy head, the cheeks, neck and chest are slim, the limbs are their real thickness, while the haunches and long hind feet stay full size because they are muscle and bone. The furred views stay the target for the surface stage. Fur depth by region, for the surface stage to grow: body and back short to medium (about a tenth of the head width); cheeks and crown medium to long (the round face and the tuft at the horn base); chest and throat long (the ruff); legs short, feet short with fuller fur around the pads; ears short on the outer face with a slightly longer fringe at the edges and tips; tail very long and radiating in every direction from the stub, forming the cotton ball. The two earlier bare-body versions (furred, then clay of the furred silhouette) are retired.
